topic.title: Neural Loss Geometry and Implicit Learning Bias
topic.overview: Neural optimization is nonconvex, yet wide networks often fit their training data efficiently. This topic studies how width, depth, initialization, nonsmooth activations, and gradient dynamics shape that behavior. It also asks which solutions training prefers and how properties such as margins or local sensitivity relate to learned representations.
topic.whyItMatters: Successful interpolation does not by itself explain generalization or robustness. The geometry that permits optimization and the bias that selects among solutions are distinct pieces of a useful theory.
topic.evolution: Early representatives analyze nonsmooth learning and online gradient dynamics. Later work proves convergence under overparameterization and studies simplicity bias in shallow networks. Recent papers characterize local minima, linear-region structure, depth-dependent bias, and width-independent sensitivity bounds in specified initialization or lazy-training regimes.
openQuestions: Which conclusions extend beyond highly overparameterized or lazy-training settings?
How do optimization-friendly landscapes interact with robustness and the complexity of the learned function?

papers.title: How regularization affects the critical points in linear networks

papers.title: Learning ReLUs via Gradient Descent

papers.title: Invariance of Weight Distributions in Rectified MLPs

papers.title: On the Power of Over-parametrization in Neural Networks with Quadratic Activation

papers.title: Optimization Landscape and Expressivity of Deep CNNs

papers.title: Understanding the Loss Surface of Neural Networks for Binary Classification

papers.title: Are ResNets Provably Better than Linear Predictors?

papers.title: How to Start Training: The Effect of Initialization and Architecture

papers.title: Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Linear Convolutional Networks

papers.title: Porcupine Neural Networks: Approximating Neural Network Landscapes

papers.title: A Convergence Theory for Deep Learning via Over-Parameterization
papers.tldr: Under nondegenerate inputs and sufficient overparameterization, stochastic gradient descent can globally optimize deep networks’ training objectives in polynomial time.

papers.title: Global Convergence of Block Coordinate Descent in Deep Learning
papers.tldr: The paper establishes O(1/k) convergence to a critical point for broad classes of block coordinate descent methods used in deep learning.

papers.title: Gradient Descent Finds Global Minima of Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: For the studied over-parameterized residual networks, Gram-matrix stability yields a polynomial-time guarantee of zero training loss under gradient descent.

papers.title: On Connected Sublevel Sets in Deep Learning
papers.tldr: A class of over-parameterized, piecewise-linear networks has connected, unbounded loss sublevel sets and one connected global valley.

papers.title: Toward Understanding the Importance of Noise in Training Neural Networks
papers.tldr: For a simple two-layer CNN, perturbed gradient descent with noise annealing provably reaches a global optimum in polynomial time from arbitrary initialization.

papers.title: Why do Larger Models Generalize Better? A Theoretical Perspective via the XOR Problem
papers.tldr: In a specific convolutional-network setting, extra parameters improve generalization through the interaction of initial feature exploration and weight clustering.

papers.title: Are deep ResNets provably better than linear predictors?
papers.tldr: Under geometric conditions, deep ResNet critical points either match the best linear predictor or possess a direction of negative curvature.

papers.title: Asymmetric Valleys: Beyond Sharp and Flat Local Minima
papers.tldr: Under mild assumptions, moving toward the flatter side of an asymmetric loss valley improves generalization, and weight averaging induces such a bias.

papers.title: Explaining Landscape Connectivity of Low-cost Solutions for Multilayer Nets

papers.title: Fast Convergence of Natural Gradient Descent for Over-Parameterized Neural Networks

papers.title: Gradient Dynamics of Shallow Univariate ReLU Networks

papers.title: How degenerate is the parametrization of neural networks with the ReLU activation function?
papers.tldr: The paper identifies obstacles to connecting ReLU parameter optimization with function-space optimization and establishes a restricted stability result for shallow networks.

papers.title: Implicit Regularization of Discrete Gradient Dynamics in Linear Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Under vanishing initialization and small steps, a two-layer linear network learns reduced-rank regression solutions in increasing rank order.

papers.title: Initialization of ReLUs for Dynamical Isometry
papers.tldr: An exact analysis of Gaussian-initialized networks motivates initial parameter sharing to address standard ReLU initialization's lack of dynamical isometry.

papers.title: Large Scale Structure of Neural Network Loss Landscapes

papers.title: Learning and Generalization in Overparameterized Neural Networks, Going Beyond Two Layers

papers.title: Learning Distributions Generated by One-Layer ReLU Networks

papers.title: Limitations of Lazy Training of Two-layers Neural Network
papers.tldr: For the studied quadratic networks, restricted training can have a potentially unbounded risk gap when network width is below input dimension.

papers.title: On Lazy Training in Differentiable Programming

papers.title: On Learning Over-parameterized Neural Networks: A Functional Approximation Perspective

papers.title: Piecewise Strong Convexity of Neural Networks

papers.title: Regularization Matters: Generalization and Optimization of Neural Nets v.s. their Induced Kernel

papers.title: Semi-flat minima and saddle points by embedding neural networks to overparameterization

papers.title: Towards Understanding the Importance of Shortcut Connections in Residual Networks

papers.title: Geometry of the Loss Landscape in Overparameterized Neural Networks: Symmetries and Invariances

papers.title: On Learnability via Gradient Method for Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks in Teacher-Student Setting

papers.title: Robust Implicit Networks via Non-Euclidean Contractions

papers.title: The Implicit Bias of Minima Stability: A View from Function Space
papers.tldr: For single-hidden-layer univariate ReLU networks, SGD stability biases converged functions toward greater smoothness as the learning rate increases.

papers.title: When Are Solutions Connected in Deep Networks?

papers.title: Fast Convex Optimization for Two-Layer ReLU Networks: Equivalent Model Classes and Cone Decompositions
papers.tldr: Convex reformulations and specialized solvers make two-layer ReLU training faster in the reported comparisons, with exact or approximate relationships depending on regularization.

papers.title: Reverse Engineering the Neural Tangent Kernel
papers.tldr: Choosing an activation function can realize any positive-semidefinite dot-product kernel as a one-hidden-layer network’s NNGP or neural tangent kernel.

papers.title: What Can Linear Interpolation of Neural Network Loss Landscapes Tell Us?

papers.title: A Combinatorial Perspective on the Optimization of Shallow ReLU Networks

papers.title: Annihilation of Spurious Minima in Two-Layer ReLU Networks

papers.title: Blessing of Depth in Linear Regression: Deeper Models Have Flatter Landscape Around the True Solution

papers.title: Convergence beyond the over-parameterized regime using Rayleigh quotients
papers.tldr: Rayleigh quotients provide a unified route to gradient-flow convergence proofs without requiring infinite parameter counts or finite sample sets.

papers.title: Exact Solutions of a Deep Linear Network
papers.tldr: Exact analysis of a deep linear network shows that weight decay can create bad zero-valued minima when the network has multiple hidden layers.

papers.title: Feature Learning in $L_2$-regularized DNNs: Attraction/Repulsion and Sparsity
papers.tldr: Rewriting regularized neural-network losses in terms of representations reveals feature-learning structure and quadratic worst-case bounds on hidden-layer width.

papers.title: Gradient flow dynamics of shallow ReLU networks for square loss and orthogonal inputs
papers.tldr: For shallow ReLU networks with orthogonal inputs and small initialization, the paper characterizes zero-loss convergence, implicit bias, and saddle-to-saddle training dynamics.

papers.title: Is this the Right Neighborhood? Accurate and Query Efficient Model Agnostic Explanations
papers.tldr: Adaptive neighborhood sampling produces faithful, stable local explanations with fewer samples and black-box queries in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Learning Energy Networks with Generalized Fenchel-Young Losses
papers.tldr: Generalized Fenchel-Young losses enable efficient energy-network gradients without argmin or argmax differentiation, with calibration proved for linear-concave energies.

papers.title: Learning single-index models with shallow neural networks
papers.tldr: Shallow networks with randomly fixed biases can learn single-index models through gradient flow with near-optimal sample-complexity guarantees.

papers.title: Local Identifiability of Deep ReLU Neural Networks: the Theory
papers.tldr: A geometric representation of deep ReLU networks yields numerically testable conditions for local parameter identifiability from a sample.

papers.title: Neural Collapse with Normalized Features: A Geometric Analysis over the Riemannian Manifold
papers.tldr: Under a spherical feature model, neural-collapse solutions are the only global optima, and all other critical points are strict saddles.

papers.tldr: For a structured class of ResNets, the paper connects convergence theory to finite parameterizations satisfying an expressivity condition with high probability.

papers.title: On Margin Maximization in Linear and ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: Gradient-flow convergence to a maximum-margin KKT point need not yield even a local optimum, though some settings admit stronger guarantees.

papers.title: On the Effective Number of Linear Regions in Shallow Univariate ReLU Networks: Convergence Guarantees and Implicit Bias
papers.tldr: Under stated assumptions, gradient flow learns a perfectly fitting univariate ReLU classifier with only O(r) linear regions.

papers.title: On the non-universality of deep learning: quantifying the cost of symmetry
papers.tldr: The paper proves conditional limits on efficient neural-network learning arising from equivariant gradient training and, separately, cryptographic assumptions.

papers.tldr: Theory shows that width and depth can help or hurt average robustness depending on parameterization, initialization, and training regime.

papers.tldr: The paper connects early neural-network weight condensation under small initialization to the activation function's root multiplicity at zero.

papers.title: Global Convergence Analysis of Local SGD for Two-layer Neural Network without Overparameterization
papers.tldr: For two-layer networks with Gaussian inputs, the paper proves local SGD can reach a global minimum without overparameterization or injected noise.

papers.title: Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent for Two-layer ReLU and Leaky ReLU Networks on Nearly-orthogonal Data
papers.tldr: On nearly orthogonal data, gradient descent favors bounded stable rank and asymptotically equal normalized margins in two-layer ReLU-family networks.

papers.title: Learning a Neuron by a Shallow ReLU Network: Dynamics and Implicit Bias for Correlated Inputs
papers.tldr: For the studied correlated-input setting, gradient flow learns a single neuron with a shallow ReLU network while favoring low-rank parameters.

papers.title: Minimum norm interpolation by perceptra: Explicit regularization and implicit bias
papers.tldr: Shallow ReLU risk minimizers converge to minimum-norm interpolants when weight decay vanishes at a precise rate as data and network size grow.

papers.title: On the spectral bias of two-layer linear networks
papers.tldr: For a specified initialization shape, small-scale initialization biases gradient-flow training of two-layer linear networks toward low-rank hidden representations.

papers.title: Path Regularization: A Convexity and Sparsity Inducing Regularization for Parallel ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: Pathwise regularization reveals exact convex, group-sparse formulations of parallel ReLU network training and supports an approximate algorithm with global optimality guarantees.

papers.title: Penalising the biases in norm regularisation enforces sparsity
papers.tldr: For one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on one-dimensional data, penalizing biases enforces a unique minimum-norm interpolator with sparse slope changes.

papers.title: Principled Weight Initialisation for Input-Convex Neural Networks
papers.tldr: An initialization derived for nonnegative weights accelerates input-convex network learning and improves generalization in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Training shallow ReLU networks on noisy data using hinge loss: when do we overfit and is it benign?
papers.tldr: Margin conditions distinguish benign, harmful, and avoided overfitting in shallow ReLU networks trained on lightly corrupted labels.

papers.title: Understanding Multi-phase Optimization Dynamics and Rich Nonlinear Behaviors of ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: A full analysis of two-layer ReLU training under gradient flow reveals four phases and captures nonlinear behavior from initialization to convergence.

papers.title: A Global Geometric Analysis of Maximal Coding Rate Reduction
papers.tldr: Every MCR² maximizer yields a compact, discriminative, diverse representation, and every other critical point is a strict saddle.

papers.title: Activation-Descent Regularization for Input Optimization of ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: Differentiable representations of ReLU activation patterns help guide input updates with improved local descent properties.

papers.title: Convex Relaxations of ReLU Neural Networks Approximate Global Optima in Polynomial Time
papers.tldr: For random data, convex relaxations yield polynomial-time approximation guarantees for training weight-decayed two-layer ReLU networks.

papers.title: Deconstructing the Goldilocks Zone of Neural Network Initialization
papers.tldr: The paper explains positive curvature near certain initializations and finds that this Goldilocks zone does not perfectly track strong model performance.

papers.title: Expand-and-Cluster: Parameter Recovery of Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Training oversized imitators and clustering their shared weights can recover network sizes and weights, subject to activation-dependent sign or scaling ambiguities.

papers.title: Monotone, Bi-Lipschitz, and Polyak-Łojasiewicz Networks
papers.tldr: BiLipNet controls an invertible network's sensitivity and distinguishability, while PLNet uses it to construct nonconvex losses with a unique, efficiently computable global minimum.

papers.title: On a Neural Implementation of Brenier’s Polar Factorization
papers.tldr: The paper implements Brenier’s vector-field factorization with neural networks and explores its use in optimization and sampling.

papers.title: Subhomogeneous Deep Equilibrium Models
papers.tldr: Subhomogeneous operator theory establishes fixed-point existence and uniqueness for implicit networks under weaker parameter-matrix assumptions than related analyses.

papers.title: Universal Consistency of Wide and Deep ReLU Neural Networks and Minimax Optimal Convergence Rates for Kolmogorov-Donoho Optimal Function Classes
papers.tldr: The paper proves consistency for wide and deep ReLU classifiers and gives sufficient conditions for minimax-optimal convergence rates.

papers.title: A New Neural Kernel Regime: The Inductive Bias of Multi-Task Learning
papers.tldr: Multi-task learning in minimum-weight shallow ReLU networks produces kernel-like solutions, with almost-always uniqueness proved for single-variable inputs.

papers.title: Bayes-optimal learning of an extensive-width neural network from quadratically many samples
papers.tldr: For a large random network with quadratic activations, the paper derives Bayes-optimal test error and an algorithm that asymptotically achieves it.

papers.title: Benign overfitting in leaky ReLU networks with moderate input dimension
papers.tldr: Under a structured signal-and-noise model, leaky ReLU networks can overfit benignly at input dimensions that grow only linearly with sample size.

papers.title: $\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{P^2}$: Effective Sharpness Aware Minimization Requires Layerwise Perturbation Scaling
papers.tldr: μP² scales SAM perturbations by layer so all layers remain effectively perturbed and feature-learning at infinite width.

papers.title: Deep linear networks for regression are implicitly regularized towards flat minima
papers.tldr: Under the studied initializations, gradient flow in deep linear regression networks selects minima within a data-dependent constant factor of the sharpness lower bound.

papers.title: Guiding Neural Collapse: Optimising Towards the Nearest Simplex Equiangular Tight Frame
papers.tldr: Setting classifier weights to the nearest symmetric simplex geometry during training accelerates convergence and improves stability in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Loss Landscape Characterization of Neural Networks without Over-Parametrization
papers.tldr: A new loss-landscape assumption permits saddle points and yields conditional convergence guarantees without requiring extensive network over-parameterization.

papers.title: Mean-Field Analysis for Learning Subspace-Sparse Polynomials with Gaussian Input
papers.tldr: A mean-field analysis gives closely related necessary and sufficient conditions for learning subspace-sparse polynomials under Gaussian inputs.

papers.title: Neural Characteristic Activation Analysis and Geometric Parameterization for ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: Geometric Parameterization separates weight magnitude and direction to resolve an identified ReLU-training instability, with empirical benefits for training and generalization.

papers.title: Neural collapse vs. low-rank bias: Is deep neural collapse really optimal?
papers.tldr: In the studied deep unconstrained features model, multilayer regularization favors lower-rank solutions over deep neural collapse beyond simpler settings.

papers.title: Only Strict Saddles in the Energy Landscape of Predictive Coding Networks?
papers.tldr: Predictive-coding inference provably makes many saddles easier to escape in deep linear networks, with experiments suggesting a broader effect.

papers.title: Optimal deep learning of holomorphic operators between Banach spaces
papers.tldr: The paper establishes near-unimprovable generalization guarantees for neural learning of holomorphic operators between Banach spaces.

papers.title: Precise asymptotics of reweighted least-squares algorithms for linear diagonal networks
papers.tldr: A unified analysis shows how suitable reweighting can yield rapid progress and exploit group sparsity to improve test error.

papers.title: Stable Minima Cannot Overfit in Univariate ReLU Networks: Generalization by Large Step Sizes
papers.tldr: For noisy one-dimensional regression, stability under fixed-step gradient descent constrains ReLU fits and yields near-optimal generalization under stated assumptions.

papers.title: The Prevalence of Neural Collapse in Neural Multivariate Regression
papers.tldr: Neural Regression Collapse links final-layer feature and weight geometry to target structure, with a regularized theoretical model explaining the observed patterns.

papers.title: Theoretical Characterisation of the Gauss Newton Conditioning in Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper derives tight Gauss-Newton conditioning bounds for deep linear networks and extends the analysis to selected nonlinear and architectural settings.

papers.title: Topological obstruction to the training of shallow ReLU neural networks
papers.tldr: For shallow scalar-output ReLU networks, initialization-dependent disconnected constraints can prevent gradient flow from reaching a global optimum.

papers.title: Understanding Representation of Deep Equilibrium Models from Neural Collapse Perspective
papers.tldr: Neural-collapse analysis reveals structured representations in deep equilibrium models and conditional geometric advantages under class imbalance.

papers.title: A Bregman Proximal Viewpoint on Neural Operators
papers.tldr: An optimization-based interpretation of neural operators leads to a Bregman variant with equal expressivity and experimentally supported benefits for depth and accuracy.

papers.title: Compelling ReLU Networks to Exhibit Exponentially Many Linear Regions at Initialization and During Training
papers.tldr: A constrained parameterization preserves exactly 2^d linear regions in depth-d ReLU networks and greatly improves convex one-dimensional function approximation.

papers.title: Enforcing Idempotency in Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A matrix-derived training update helps neural networks become idempotent, reducing repeated-application error across tested architectures.

papers.title: Global curvature for second-order optimization of neural networks
papers.tldr: Neural network symmetries expose a compact global-curvature structure that enables faster second-order optimization in synthetic experiments.

papers.title: Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent for Non-Homogeneous Deep Networks
papers.tldr: Under near-homogeneity and sufficiently low initial risk, gradient descent converges in direction toward a KKT point of a margin maximization problem.

papers.title: Neural Collapse Beyond the Unconstrained Features Model: Landscape, Dynamics, and Generalization in the Mean-Field Regime
papers.tldr: In a mean-field network setting, small loss and gradient norm imply approximate NC1, with generalization results for well-separated data.

papers.title: On the Local Complexity of Linear Regions in Deep ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: A measure of local linear-region density links low-dimensional ReLU representations to functional variation and adversarial robustness.

papers.title: Optimization for Neural Operators can Benefit from Width
papers.tldr: A unified analysis gives gradient-descent convergence guarantees for two neural-operator families and shows how greater width can benefit training.

papers.title: Simplicity Bias and Optimization Threshold in Two-Layer ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: Early neuron alignment can steer overparameterized two-layer ReLU networks toward simpler solutions that improve test loss without interpolating training data.

papers.title: Transformative or Conservative? Conservation laws for ResNets and Transformers
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes conservation laws in neural-network building blocks and shows how local parameter laws can be studied in isolation.

papers.title: Understanding Mode Connectivity via Parameter Space Symmetry
papers.tldr: Parameter-space symmetries explain aspects of connected neural network minima and yield conditions for approximate straight-line connectivity.

papers.title: Block Coordinate Descent for Neural Networks Provably Finds Global Minima
papers.tldr: The paper proves global convergence for a neural-network block coordinate descent algorithm under strictly increasing activations and extends the result to a modified ReLU version.

papers.title: Composing Global Solutions to Reasoning Tasks via Algebraic Objects in Neural Nets
papers.tldr: For a specific class of reasoning networks, algebraic operations combine partial solutions into global optima and help explain training behavior.

papers.title: Embedding Principle of Homogeneous Neural Network for Classification Problem
papers.tldr: Specific neuron and channel splitting transformations preserve maximum-margin KKT points and mapped gradient-flow dynamics across network widths.

papers.title: Generalization Bounds for Rank-sparse Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper derives generalization bounds that exploit approximately low-rank weights and improve on conventional bounds in reported overparametrised settings.

papers.title: $\mu$PC: Scaling Predictive Coding to 100+ Layer Networks
papers.tldr: μPC enables stable predictive-coding training of residual networks up to 128 layers on simple classification tasks and transfers learning rates across sizes.

papers.title: Neural Collapse under Gradient Flow on Shallow ReLU Networks for Orthogonally Separable Data
papers.tldr: The paper proves neural collapse under gradient flow for two-layer ReLU classifiers with orthogonally separable data.

papers.title: Non-Singularity of the Gradient Descent Map for Neural Networks with Piecewise Analytic Activations
papers.tldr: The paper proves gradient descent map non-singularity for practical neural architectures with piecewise analytic activations at almost all step sizes.

papers.title: Optimal Rates for Generalization of Gradient Descent for Deep ReLU Classification
papers.tldr: Under NTK separability, gradient descent for deep ReLU classifiers achieves optimal sample-size generalization rates up to polynomial depth factors.

papers.title: SAD Neural Networks: Divergent Gradient Flows and Asymptotic Optimality via o-minimal Structures
papers.tldr: Under stated conditions, neural-network gradient flows can approach optimal loss while their parameters necessarily diverge.

papers.title: Stable Minima of ReLU Neural Networks Suffer from the Curse of Dimensionality: The Neural Shattering Phenomenon
papers.tldr: For the studied two-layer ReLU networks, flatness-based generalization rates worsen exponentially with input dimension, unlike known low-norm guarantees.

papers.title: The Nuclear Route: Sharp Asymptotics of ERM in Overparameterized Quadratic Networks
papers.tldr: A convex matrix-sensing reformulation yields precise high-dimensional error and learnability results for regularized, overparameterized quadratic networks.

papers.title: The Persistence of Neural Collapse Despite Low-Rank Bias
papers.tldr: The paper argues that deep neural collapse remains common because of its prevalence in the loss landscape despite low-rank optimality bias.

papers.title: On the Infinite Width and Depth Limits of Predictive Coding Networks
papers.tldr: Stable scaling lets linear predictive-coding networks approach backpropagation gradients at equilibrium when width grows much faster than depth.

papers.title: Path-conditioned training: a principled way to rescale ReLU neural networks
papers.tldr: A geometric rescaling method exploits ReLU parameter symmetries and shows potential to speed up training.

papers.title: Sharp description of local minima in the loss landscape of high-dimensional two-layer ReLU neural networks
papers.tldr: An exact summary-statistic description links local minima to SGD dynamics in Gaussian teacher–student ReLU networks and explains effects of overparameterization.

papers.title: The Implicit Bias of Depth: From Neural Collapse to Softmax Codes
papers.tldr: In deep unconstrained feature models, depth implicitly favors low-rank alternatives to neural collapse, while increased width can favor higher rank.

papers.title: Width Independent Bounds for the Local Lipschitz Constant of Deep Neural Networks at Random Initialization and after Lazy Training
papers.tldr: For smooth-activation networks, finite-width local Lipschitz bounds remain independent of width at initialization and throughout lazy training.
